guidance.outlook: No numerical guidance ('we typically don't make forward statements'); Q2 business on books 'very positive' vs last year; foreign arrivals expected to stay weak in Q2 and hoped to recover in Q3-Q4 (12-Aug-2026 call).
guidance.margins: Renovations continue in Q2; 'in Q3 and Q4 there will be really no significant renovation'; FY27 'should look much more better' on margin and growth (agreed on the 29-May-2026 call).
guidance.capex: Rs600-700 cr a year 'in the next one or two years', higher towards FY29-30 when bigger hotels come in (29-May-2026 call); CARE: ~Rs500-600 cr a year, no debt envisaged.
guidance.rajgarh: Leisure hotels take ~3 years to stabilise (12-Aug-2026 call).
guidance.pipeline: ~30 new properties (owned, JV and managed) by 2031.

mashobra: Wildflower Hall (85 keys, Shimla) was owned by Mashobra Resort Ltd, a 1995 JV with the Himachal Pradesh government. After the Supreme Court order (20-Feb-2024) EIH handed the hotel to the State on 31-Mar-2025; Mashobra Resort ceased to be a subsidiary. High Court orders (2-Jun and 14-Oct 2025) set the compensation; EIH's shares were transferred to the State in Dec-2025 and the proceedings closed on 5-Jan-2026. EIH runs the hotel under interim operation and maintenance arrangements (six months to October 2026, per the CFO on 29-May-2026) while the State runs an auction for a long-term operator; EIH is bidding (qualifying-bid date moved to 10-Sep-2026; a live auction follows). Outcome unknown at 30-Sep-2026.

history: Oberoi group founded by M.S. Oberoi in the 1930s (CARE); the company was incorporated in West Bengal in 1949 as The East India Hotels Ltd (CIN L55101WB1949PLC017981), absorbed The Associated Hotels of India and was later renamed EIH Ltd (AR FY26 title-deed note)
Joint venture with the Himachal Pradesh government; Mashobra Resort acquires the Wildflower Hall property in 1997 (AR FY26 note 47A)
Two strategic outside holders: Reliance Strategic Business Ventures (Reliance Industries) 18.83% and ITC Ltd 16.13% at Jun-2026; Nita M. Ambani sits on the board as a non-independent director
Covid: revenue Rs494 cr and an operating loss of Rs354 cr in FY21; loss of Rs34 cr in FY22. Equity capital Rs114 cr -> Rs125 cr in FY21 (62.54 cr shares of Rs2 since)
Turnaround: revenue Rs2,019 cr, operating EBITDA Rs599 cr (30% margin), attributable profit Rs315 cr; bank debt repaid by FY24

P.R.S. Oberoi dies; Arjun Singh Oberoi becomes Executive Chairman, Vikramjit Singh Oberoi MD & CEO. A dispute over the promoter shareholding within the family is reported in 2025 (CARE: under legal consideration, a monitorable)

Supreme Court orders Wildflower Hall handed to the Himachal government (done 31-Mar-2025); FY26 exceptional charge net Rs102 cr on Mashobra; EIH runs it on an interim contract and bids in the 2026 auction

Revenue Rs2,743 cr -> Rs2,940 cr; operating margin 37.5% -> 34.8%; The Oberoi Grand Kolkata (209 keys) and Trident Jaipur close for renovation; The Oberoi Rajgarh Palace (65 keys) opens Nov-2025; Rs330 cr paid to convert the Mumbai land to freehold
CARE assigns an AA+ (Stable) issuer rating

accounting.leases: Lease liabilities Rs199 cr (Mar-26) are the only debt; lease rent of Rs50 cr is still expensed for short or variable leases.
accounting.renovation: Renovation costs are capitalised; the undepreciated value of replaced assets is written off through the P&L (Q1FY27 Rs7.5 cr).
